text: Welcome to Neel's Night Party! Help Neel plan a party, when he has not decided how many friends will come.
I want to have a party next week!
Yay! How many friends are coming?
Umm… I don't know. I have not decided yet.
Then how will we plan? How many plates? How many sweets?
Don't worry. When we don't know a number, we can write it as a letter.
Neel's friends are monsters. So we use the letter m, for monsters. m is the number of Neel's monster friends.
m is a variable, because we don't know the number of friends yet. It can change.
When Neel decides who is coming, we can easily find the exact number of things we need.
m? Okay! Let's plan!
It's party day! Knock knock! The friends are here!
Look! 4 of my monster friends are here!
And 7 of my dragon friends are here too!
My friends changed their minds, but our plan still worked!
That is because m and d can be any number. That is why we use variables. Well done!
Let's party!
The party begins! Neel and all the friends dance all night.
agni
My party list is checked!
Things that change with the number of friends are variables.
Things that stay the same are constants.
Now let's write the party plan!
My party plan is ready!
But how many things do we really need to buy?
We can find out as soon as you decide how many friends are coming.
Okay. Let me decide!
Yay! Now I know exactly what we need!
Even when the numbers changed, the plan still worked!
That is the magic of variables. m and d can be any number.
Some numbers depend on how many friends come. If more friends come, they change. A number that can change is a variable.
Some numbers stay the same, however many friends come. A number that stays the same is a constant.
Turn the magic dial to change the friends. Watch what changes. Then put each thing in the jar or the chest!
Not yet.
Try again.
Let's see the answer together.
Wait! My dragon friends are also coming!
Hmm… it worked for 1 and 1. But not for the others!
Oh no! My spell gives the wrong number of candles!
Then we need a second letter. m is for monsters, so let's use d for dragons. d is the number of Agni's dragon friends.
And don't forget me. I will need 1 extra of some things too!
Now we write a plan for m monster friends. Each friend gets 2 sweets.
For m friends it is m × 2. We write it short as 2m. A number next to a letter means multiply.
Words give clues. Each means multiply.
Extra means add.
Broke means take away.
Tap the orbs to brew a spell. Then tap Brew! and the cauldron will test it.
Take your time.
That spell is not finished. Every + or × needs something on both sides.
Let's brew it together.
maya
I have decided! 6 monster friends are coming. Tap the door to let them in!
So now m is 6. To find the exact number, put 6 in place of m in the plan. Then work it out.
For example, glasses: 2 for each friend is 2m. Put 6 in place of m: 2 × 6 = 12 glasses. Now you try!
Let's see it together.
Now we know the real numbers: 4 monsters and 7 dragons. Let's get everything ready!
Let's work it out step by step. Look at the plan.
Here it is:
Yes! That is right.
Super! You got it right.
Great job! That is correct.
Well done! You got it.
Number of friends coming to the party.
Neel has not decided yet. It can be 5 or 10. So the number of friends is a variable.
Not yet. Try again.
Has Neel decided how many friends will come?
It can be 5. It can be 10. Is it the same every time?
Has Neel decided yet?
Turn the dial.
Tap Variable or Constant.
Number of cakes. I will cut one big cake, however many friends come.
There is always 1 big cake, however many friends come. So the number of cakes is a constant.
Read it again: one big cake, however many friends come.
5 friends: 1 cake. 10 friends: still 1 cake. Does it change?
One big cake for everyone.
Number of plates. One plate for each friend.
One plate for each friend. If the friends change, the plates change too. So the number of plates is a variable.
If more friends come, do we need more plates?
5 friends need 5 plates. 10 friends need 10 plates.
One plate for each friend.
Number of lamps in the hall. The hall has 6 lamps.
The hall always has 6 lamps. It does not depend on the friends. So the number of lamps is a constant.
Does the hall get more lamps when more friends come?
5 friends: 6 lamps. 8 friends: still 6 lamps.
Count the lamps as you turn the dial.
Number of sweets in one box. Every box has 10 sweets.
Every box has 10 sweets. It never changes. So the sweets in a box is a constant.
Read it again: every box has 10 sweets.
Turn the dial. Does one box ever get more sweets?
Every box has 10 sweets.
Number of boxes of sweets. I need enough sweets for all my friends.
If more friends come, Neel needs more boxes. So the number of boxes is a variable.
More friends need more sweets. Do they need more boxes?
Turn the dial up. Watch the boxes.
Watch the boxes as the friends change.
Number of balloons on the door. Neel puts 10 balloons on the door.
The door always gets 10 balloons. They do not depend on the friends. So this number is a constant.
These balloons are only for the door. Do they depend on the friends?
2 friends: 10 balloons. 8 friends: still 10.
These balloons are for the door.
Number of balloons to give away. One balloon for each friend.
One balloon for each friend. If the friends change, these balloons change. Same balloons, but a different use! So this is a variable.
Now the balloons are for the friends. One for each friend.
Turn the dial. More friends, more balloons?
One balloon for each friend.
Now you know! Let's check the next thing.
Chairs: one chair for each friend, and 1 extra chair for me. How many chairs for m friends?
One chair for each friend is m chairs. 1 extra chair for Neel means add 1. So the chairs are m + 1.
Look at the test. Each time, we take the number of friends and add 1.
Extra means add. Try m, then +, then 1.
Sweets: each friend gets 3 sweets. How many sweets for m friends?
Each friend gets 3 sweets, so we multiply: m × 3. We write it short as 3m.
Each time, we multiply the number of friends by 3.
Each means multiply. A number next to a letter means multiply: 3m.
Cups: one cup for each friend. Oops! Neel broke 2 cups. How many cups are left?
There was one cup for each friend, so m cups. 2 cups broke, so we take away 2. Now there are m − 2 cups.
Neel had one cup for each friend, so m cups. Then 2 cups broke.
Broke means take away. Try m − 2.
Candles: 4 candles for each friend. I wrote 4 + m. Am I right? Tap Brew to test my spell!
4 candles for each friend means 4 × m, which we write as 4m. So Neel was not right.
4 candles for each friend. Does each mean add or multiply?
Each means multiply. Clear Neel's spell and try 4m.
Balloons: 2 balloons for each friend, and 5 more for the door. How many balloons?
2 balloons for each friend is 2m. Then we add 5 for the door. So we need 2m + 5 balloons.
Do it in two steps. First, balloons for the friends: 2 for each friend.
First 2m. Then add 5 for the door.
m monster friends and d dragon friends are coming. How many friends in all?
In all means add. m monsters and d dragons make m + d friends in all.
In all means add the two groups.
Monsters plus dragons: m + d.
Plates: one plate for each friend, and 1 extra plate for Maya. How many plates?
One plate for each friend is m + d plates. 1 extra for Maya means add 1. So the plates are m + d + 1.
First, one plate for each friend. All the friends are m + d.
m + d, then add 1 for Maya.
Cushions: each monster needs 1 cushion. Dragons are big, so each dragon needs 2 cushions. How many in all?
Monsters need m cushions. Dragons need 2d cushions. In all means add. So the cushions are m + 2d.
Monster cushions: 1 for each monster is m. Dragon cushions: 2 for each dragon.
m for monsters, 2d for dragons. Add them.
Laddoos: each monster gets 3 laddoos and each dragon gets 2 laddoos. How many in total?
Monsters get 3m laddoos. Dragons get 2d laddoos. Total means add. So the laddoos are 3m + 2d.
Monster laddoos: 3 for each monster is 3m.
3m for monsters, 2d for dragons. Total means add.
I think 3m + 2d is the same as 5md. Am I right? Tap Brew to test my spell!
m and d are different numbers, so we cannot join 3m and 2d together. 3m + 2d is already as short as it can be. Neel is not right.
m is the number of monsters. d is the number of dragons. Are they the same thing?
Chairs = m + 1. Neel decided m is 6. Tap the gold m to open it!
Put 6 in place of m: 6 + 1 = 7. So Neel needs 7 chairs.
Put 6 in place of m.
Sweets = 3m. m is 6. How many sweets?
3m means 3 × m. Put 6 in place of m: 3 × 6 = 18 sweets. 3m does not mean 36.
3m means 3 × m.
Balloons = 2m + 5. m is 6. How many balloons?
2m is 2 × 6 = 12. Then add 5: 12 + 5 = 17 balloons.
First work out 2m. Then add 5.
And 4 of my dragon friends are coming! Friends in all = m + d. How many friends?
Put 6 in place of m and 4 in place of d: 6 + 4 = 10 friends in all.
Put 6 in place of m and 4 in place of d.
Plates = m + d + 1. How many plates?
Put 6 in place of m and 4 in place of d: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11 plates.
m is 6 and d is 4. Don't forget the 1 extra plate for Maya.
Oh no! 2 of my friends said no. Now how many monster friends are coming?
6 friends were coming. 2 said no, so 6 − 2 = 4. Now m is 4. See? m can change!
Said no means they are not coming. So we take away.
Now m is 4 and d is 4. Cushions = m + 2d. How many cushions?
2d is 2 × 4 = 8. Add m: 4 + 8 = 12 cushions.
First work out 2d. Then add m.
Yay! 3 more dragon friends said yes. Now d is 4 + 3 = 7. Laddoos = 3m + 2d. How many laddoos?
3m is 3 × 4 = 12. 2d is 2 × 7 = 14. Add them: 12 + 14 = 26 laddoos. The plan still works, even when the numbers change!
m is still 4. d is now 7.
Listen! Someone is knocking!
More knocking! Who is it?
Chairs = m + 1. How many chairs do we need now?
Put 4 in place of m.
Plates = m + d + 1. How many plates?
m is 4 and d is 7. Don't forget Maya's plate.
Cushions = m + 2d. Dragons need 2 each!
First work out 2d. d is 7.
Laddoos = 3m + 2d. The last one!
3m is 3 × 4. 2d is 2 × 7. Then add.
